newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes down against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes down against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan fell for the third day in a row on Friday on speculative selling despite reduced intervention by the central bank, closing down at 8.3018 against the U.S. dollar, dealers said.

The yuan opened up at 8.3006 from Thursday's 8.3013 and hit an intra-day high of 8.3005 early in the session. It fell to move between 8.3011 and 8.3015 for the most of the session, hitting a low of 8.3022.
Trading was active, with most done at 8.3015, traders said.
"Buying failed to reverse falls of the past few days due to fears of central bank intervention, with trading dominated by speculative selling," one dealer said.
"The yuan lost strong support with no short-term stimuli for the currency," a second dealer said. "But the yuan's uptrend will not change."
Dealer expect the yuan to test the 8.3000 resistance level early next week after a correction in the past few days.
The yuan closed down slightly at an intra-day low of 7.4550 from 7.4386 against 100 Japanese yen and down at 1.0735 from 1.0732 against the Hong Kong dollar.
